_doc: CODEOWNERS matching oracle. Three independent grounds of truth for any ship touching CODEOWNERS / gitignore-style path patterns: (1) `pairs` - the reference implementation's own test corpus; (2) `github_documented` - examples from GitHub's About-code-owners page with the documented expectation quoted, which is the only PUBLISHED ground truth; (3) `line_skipping` - which malformed lines GitHub silently drops. Language-agnostic JSON on purpose.

differential_recipe._doc: Beyond fixed corpora: Go 1.24+ is present in the build sandbox and hmarr/codeowners' ROOT package builds with no network (only cmd/ needs pflag, which is unreachable). Write a driver in a difftool/ subpackage of a shallow clone, build with GOFLAGS=-mod=mod, and pipe pairs through it. Ship 003 ran 100,000 generated (pattern, path) pairs this way for zero divergences.
differential_recipe.build: GOFLAGS=-mod=mod go build -o difftool ./difftool   # root pkg only; ./... fails on proxy.golang.org
differential_recipe.must_recover_from_panics: hmarr/codeowners PANICS (index out of range [-1], match.go:47) on the pattern "/": newPattern takes the left-anchored-literal fast path, strips the slash, and then indexes prefix[len(prefix)-1] on an empty string. Any driver must recover() per pair or the whole run dies. Found by ship 003, 2026-08-04.

known_divergences.intended: buildPatternRegex's unreachable `pattern == "/"` case compiles \A\z, i.e. matches only the empty string
known_divergences.ship_003: reports no match for every path
known_divergences.impact: none for real input - a changed-file path is never empty

assert: A CODEOWNERS matcher must score 100% on `pairs`, must produce the documented winner for every `github_documented` case, and must skip exactly the `line_skipping` entries marked true. Anything less is a wrong answer wearing a verdict's clothes.

regression_notes.defect: `?` compiled to 'exactly one BYTE that is not /' instead of 'exactly one RUNE that is not /'.
regression_notes.why_it_hid: The byte/rune equivalence argument that makes a byte-stepping NFA valid holds for REPEATED constructs (.+ , [^/]+ , [^/]*) but NOT for a single non-repeated occurrence. Every pure-ASCII test passes; only a multi-byte character in the PATH exposes it.
regression_notes.lesson: Any single-occurrence byte matcher in a byte-stepping port of a rune-based engine is suspect. Fuzz with non-ASCII paths, not just non-ASCII patterns.

regression_notes.defect: Parsing and NFA emission were unmetered; a ~1 MiB pattern blocked the main thread ~3.9 s before any budgeted work started.
regression_notes.lesson: Meter every stage that costs time, not just the obvious inner loop — and prefer a WALL-CLOCK deadline to a step counter: step throughput is shape-dependent (~32M/s, ~20M/s and ~4-5M/s measured for three different shapes), so a step budget is not a time bound.

regression_notes.found: 2026-08-04, ship 003 targeted re-check (fix cycle 2; second cycle authorised in session)
regression_notes.defect: A 1,101-1,291 ms main-thread block against a page advertising ~750 ms, from in-limits input.
regression_notes.named_causes: runes() took no budget; addThread()'s epsilon-closure loop had no clock check.
regression_notes.real_cause_underneath: literalBytes() called the UTF-8 encoder ONCE PER LITERAL CHARACTER — `new TextEncoder()` per call — costing 214 ms of a 526 ms parse on a 300,000-character pattern. An ASCII code point IS its own UTF-8 byte, so the encoder was never needed for it.
regression_notes.what_a_budget_cannot_bound: Garbage collection. With the pathological patterns metered, the measured block still overshot the deadline by ~200 ms because ~1M short-lived AST and instruction objects were allocated. A work budget bounds CPU in your own loops; it cannot bound the collector. The fix was a DOMAIN bound — a CODEOWNERS pattern is a path pattern, so it is capped at the same 4,096 characters a path is — which removes the allocation-bomb class instead of metering it. Aggregate load (many rules x many paths) stays the budget's job.
regression_notes.lesson: When a metered loop still overshoots its deadline, look for (a) a per-item call that allocates, and (b) work you cannot meter at all. Do not answer either one by raising the budget.
regression_notes.measured: worst adversarial main-thread block: 3,894 ms -> 1,291 ms -> 954 ms -> 607 ms, against a 750 ms promise.
